fi-pterois-volitans.title: Volitans Lionfish (Black)
fi-pterois-volitans.summary: The classic large lionfish, here in its dark color form, with long venomous spines and fan-like pectoral fins. It hides by day and hunts at dusk and dawn.
rows: About 15 in (Saltwaterfish.com adult size); wild record 45.7 cm (18 in) TL (FishBase)
Solitary; more than one needs a big tank and fish of similar size added together
Carnivore: meaty marine foods such as krill, shrimp, silversides and squid, once or twice a day
Pacific Ocean: Cocos-Keeling Islands and Western Australia in the eastern Indian Ocean to the Marquesas and Oeno (Pitcairn group)
notes: Give live rock caves plus open space to swim.
warn: Venomous spines: a sting is like a bad bee sting. Remove any broken spine, soak the area in hot (not scalding) water for about 30 minutes and get medical care; allergic people should go straight to a doctor.
Eats any fish or crustacean that fits in its mouth.

fi-pterois-antennata.title: Antennata Lionfish (Spotfin Lionfish)
fi-pterois-antennata.summary: A mid-sized lionfish with long spotted fin rays and "antennae" above its eyes. It hides by day, hunts at night, and will eat any fish or shrimp that fits in its mouth.
rows: Aggressive predator; keep one per tank
No: corals are safe but shrimp and small fish are eaten
Carnivore: meaty foods such as shrimp, krill and silversides
Indo-Pacific: East Africa to the Marquesas, southern Japan to Australia; lagoons and seaward reefs, 2–86 m
notes: Give it caves and overhangs to rest in during the day, and fairly subdued lighting; it is most active at night.
warn: Venomous spines: a sting is very painful, like a strong bee sting. Use care when working in the tank.

fi-waspfish-red-rooster.title: Pygmy Red Rooster Waspfish
fi-waspfish-red-rooster.summary: A small, bottom-dwelling waspfish with a tall, sail-like back fin. Waspfish are related to scorpionfish and many carry venomous spines.
rows: Carnivore: small meaty foods such as mysis and chopped shrimp
Indian Ocean and western Pacific; hides on the sea floor
notes: Give it hiding places among rock on the bottom.
warn: Waspfish are often venomous: avoid touching the spines.
